name: Bangladesh
genZNote: Born in 1971, mostly delta, world's biggest mangrove forest next door — Bangladesh is proof that a young country and ancient geography can absolutely coexist.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in South Asia, almost entirely surrounded by India (west, north, east) with a short border with Myanmar in the southeast and the Bay of Bengal to the south.
Sits mostly on the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna river delta — one of the world's largest river deltas.
Home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, shared with India, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Capital: Dhaka; major port: Chittagong.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Bengali (Bangla) is the official language — the 1952 Bengali Language Movement is a foundational national memory, commemorated as International Mother Language Day (21 February).
Rich tradition of Bengali literature, music, and the Baul folk-music tradition (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary republic; unicameral Parliament (Jatiya Sangsad).
Became independent in 1971 after the Bangladesh Liberation War, separating from Pakistan (having earlier separated from India during 1947 Partition as East Pakistan).

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Member of the United Nations, SAARC, and the Commonwealth of Nations.
A major contributor of personnel to UN peacekeeping missions worldwide.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India supported Bangladesh's independence movement in 1971; the two countries share deep historical, linguistic, and cultural ties (especially with West Bengal).
Extensive river-sharing arrangements exist between the two countries, given the transboundary Ganges-Brahmaputra river system.
India is a major trading partner and source of development-related credit lines for Bangladesh.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: One of the world's largest garment/textile exporters — ready-made garments are the dominant export sector.
Agriculture (notably jute and rice) and remittances from overseas workers are also significant to the economy.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The Sundarbans mangrove forest, the Ganges delta, and being one of the world's top garment exporters.
The 1971 Liberation War and its 1952 Language Movement, both central to national identity.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Bangladeshi Taka (BDT).
One of the world's largest garment/textile exporters, a major driver of its rapidly growing economy.
Agriculture (notably rice and jute) remains central to rural livelihoods.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, shared with India, and a Bengal tiger habitat.
A low-lying delta nation highly vulnerable to flooding and sea-level rise, driving major climate-adaptation efforts.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Part of British India until 1947, then East Pakistan.
Achieved independence from Pakistan in 1971 after the Bangladesh Liberation War, with significant support from India.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1971 independence from Pakistan founded the modern state.
The 1972 Constitution established a parliamentary republic; the country has since experienced periods of both civilian and military-backed rule.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Cricket is the most popular sport, with passionate nationwide following.
Recognised for its role in microfinance innovation (Grameen Bank, Nobel Peace Prize 2006).
Rich Bengali literary and musical tradition, sharing heritage with West Bengal, India.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of SAARC; member of the UN and the Commonwealth of Nations.
A leading contributor of troops to UN peacekeeping missions worldwide.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Bangladesh is a South Asian parliamentary republic on the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, independent since 1971 after separating from Pakistan.
keyFacts: Independence: 1971 (Bangladesh Liberation War), after being East Pakistan since the 1947 Partition.
Home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest (shared with India).
One of the world's largest ready-made garment exporters.
commonConfusion: Bangladesh separated from Pakistan in 1971 — a SECOND partition, distinct from the original 1947 Partition of British India.

highYieldFacts: Bangladesh's 1971 independence war and India's role in supporting it are frequently tested facts.
The Sundarbans is shared between India and Bangladesh — don't attribute it to only one country.
commonTraps: Confusing the 1947 Partition (creating East and West Pakistan) with the 1971 Liberation War (East Pakistan becoming independent Bangladesh).
mustRemember: Bangladesh = former East Pakistan, independent since 1971.
